name: The Stillwinter Grotto
history: Highcairn hunters have long used the waterfall as a landmark when crossing the upper valleys. During an exceptionally cold winter, a hunter discovered an opening behind the frozen cascade and described an enclosed landscape of ancient trees, animal remains, and objects preserved in clear ice.
current_state: For much of the year the entrance is obscured by falling water and inaccessible under ordinary conditions. In the deepest winter, the frozen cascade exposes a narrow approach to the cavern. Frost within the deeper galleries persists even when temperatures rise outside.
inhabitants: Ordinary mountain wildlife near the waterfall. The presence of living creatures within the preserved galleries has not been established.
danger_level: Low to moderate along the approach in suitable weather; potentially severe in the cavern due to cold, ice, and uncertain supernatural conditions.
discovery: A high mountain valley reached by a seasonal hunting trail. Highcairn hunters recognize the waterfall. Brannik Froststep may guide travelers toward it when the upper trails are passable.
site_type: cave | Natural wonders; Supernatural sites | Seasonally accessible cavern behind a waterfall
points_of_interest:
Blue ice curtain; narrow ledge behind the falls; frozen woodland gallery; preserved animal bones; scattered objects of uncertain origin; a deeper chamber from which the cold appears to emanate.

Unresolved elements: Age and origin of the preserved woodland and objects; whether the cold is natural or magical; whether the cavern has other entrances; what changes, if anything, when the thaw begins.
